email.title: Email
email.description: The backend alert notifications and password-reset emails are sent through. Off by default; a control plane started with APP_SMTP_* env vars still works until this is saved.

smtp.label: SMTP
smtp.presetsLabel: Quick fill for a known provider
smtp.passwordSet: A password is already configured. Leave blank to keep it.

ses.label: AWS SES
ses.secretSet: A secret key is already configured. Leave blank to keep it.

resend.label: Resend
resend.apiKeySet: An API key is already configured. Leave blank to keep it.

test.title: Send a test email
test.description: Sends one real email through the saved backend above, the same path alert notifications and password resets use.

email.comingSoon: More notification options are coming here: custom email templates, send-rate limiting, and per-alert frequency controls.
email.channelsCta: Looking for Slack, Discord, or webhook notifications instead?

wizard.intro: Password resets and alert emails go out through an SMTP server. Enter yours, save, then send a test to a real inbox before moving on.
wizard.others: Using AWS SES or Resend instead?

orphans.title: Leftover resources
orphans.description: Containers, volumes and certificates that no app or database accounts for. They are removed automatically once they stay orphaned past the grace period. Database data volumes are never removed.
orphans.empty: Nothing left over. Every container and volume belongs to a live app or database.

reason.stale_generation: Older release of a live app

toast.dryRun_one: Dry run: {{count}} resource would be removed.
toast.dryRun_other: Dry run: {{count}} resources would be removed.

authEngine.title: Sign-in engine
authEngine.description: Sign-in, sessions, API tokens, two-factor and passkeys run on the auth library {{version}}.

iamTemplates.title: Add a policy from a template
iamTemplates.description: Pick a ready-made policy. You can attach it to a user or token now, or later from the policy list.
iamTemplates.attachIdRequired: Enter the ID to attach to, or choose Nothing yet.

aiControl.title: AI control
aiControl.description: Decide what agents and the built-in assistant may do on this instance. The server enforces this on every request, whatever the token allows.
aiControl.navDescription: Turn agent access off, read-only or on, and limit it to chosen environments.

off.label: Off
off.description: Every agent request is refused. Humans are not affected.

observe.label: Observe
observe.description: Agents can read apps, logs and metrics, but not secrets, and change nothing.

operate.label: Operate
operate.description: Agents can read, write and deploy in the environments below. They cannot use root, change secrets, backups or instance settings.

admin.label: Admin
admin.description: Agents can use any ability their token holds in the environments below. A person must still approve protected deploys.

aiControl.adminUnavailable: Admin mode needs the experimental feature ai-control to be enabled on the server.
aiControl.envKindsDescription: Applies to operate and admin. Apps with no environment count as custom.
aiControl.viewAudit: View agent activity in the audit log

revoke.title: Revoke every agent token?
revoke.description: Every token with an agent label stops working immediately. This cannot be undone. The built-in assistant keeps working.

aiControl.loadFailed: Could not load AI control settings.

tokens.emptyBody: Create a scoped, revocable credential for the CLI, CI, or an MCP integration.
tokens.name: Name

create.title: Create token
create.description: A scoped, revocable credential for the CLI, CI, or an MCP integration.
create.name: Name
create.agentTip: Label the token as issued to an AI agent, for example "Claude Code". The name is shown here and on every audit log entry the token makes, so you can tell agent changes from human ones.
create.rootExclusive: Root cannot be combined with other abilities
create.signInApproveHint: Lets this token show your sign-in codes and approve new browsers from the CLI. Root does not include it and a device login never grants it. It must expire within 30 days and is revoked when you change or reset your password or sign out your other sessions.
create.signInApproveExpiry: A token that approves sign-ins must expire within 30 days
create.signInApproveAgent: A token that approves sign-ins cannot be issued to an agent
create.secretsRevealHint: Lets this token read a secret value, but only when the server allows token reveal (APP_SECRET_REVEAL_TOKENS=on) and the request carries your password. Every reveal is audited. Root does not include it.

hostFirewall.title: Host firewall
hostFirewall.description: Turns this server's ufw firewall on or off. Turning it on first allows SSH, the control plane ports and HTTP/3, so you cannot lock yourself out.
hostFirewall.confirmOnBody: These commands will run on this server, in order. SSH is allowed before the firewall is switched on.
hostFirewall.confirmOffBody: All ports on this server will be reachable again. This runs:
hostFirewall.missingHelp: Install ufw on this server to manage its firewall from here, or use your cloud provider's firewall.
hostFirewall.sshNote: SSH is on a different port? Set APP_FIREWALL_SSH_PORTS on the control plane before turning this on.

email.title: Set up outgoing email
email.description: Password resets and alert emails need an SMTP server. Pick your provider, then send a test.

alerts.title: Set up alerts
alerts.description: Get a Slack, Discord, email, or webhook message when a deploy fails.

backups.title: Add a backup target
backups.description: Point database and volume backups at S3-compatible storage.

team.title: Invite your team
team.description: Give teammates their own accounts instead of sharing yours.

databaseUpgrades.title: Database upgrades
databaseUpgrades.description: The default upgrade policy for every database that does not set its own.
databaseUpgrades.loadFailed: Could not load the platform upgrade policy: {{error}}
databaseUpgrades.formDescription: Databases inherit this until you override them on their Upgrades tab. Only the platform owner can change it.

githubApp.manageAccessHint: Missing a repository? Choose which repositories this app can see on GitHub, then come back.

owner.legend: Who owns the App on GitHub
owner.orgHelp: The organization you want to deploy from. You need permission to create GitHub Apps there.
owner.orgInvalid: Use the organization's login: letters, numbers and hyphens, up to 39 characters.
owner.allowOthers: Allow other accounts and organizations to install it
owner.publicHelp: Any GitHub account or organization can install this App. Pick this when you deploy from several organizations.
owner.privatePersonalHelp: Private: the App can only be installed on your personal account. Choose an organization above, or allow other accounts, to deploy from an organization.
owner.privateOrgHelp: Private: the App can only be installed on this organization. Allow other accounts to also install it on your personal account or other organizations.

preview.title: Review before connecting to GitHub
preview.description: GitHub's own confirmation page only lets you rename the App; everything else below is fixed before your browser leaves this page.
preview.instanceHelp: Leave blank for github.com. Self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server instances work too, e.g. https://github.example.com.
preview.appNameHelp: The one field GitHub itself lets you change on its own confirmation page too.

githubApp.notInstalled: The App was created but has not been installed on an account or organization yet. Finish installing it on GitHub to pick repositories. A private App can only be installed on the account or organization that owns it.

dockerGuard.title: Docker API guard
dockerGuard.description: Every Docker request this control plane makes passes through an allowlist that blocks privileged containers, host namespaces and protected host mounts.

enforce.label: Enforce
enforce.description: Reject requests a rule denies before they reach Docker.

audit.label: Audit
audit.description: Allow everything and record what enforce would deny.

off.label: Off
off.description: No guard. Takes effect after a restart.

dockerGuard.notConfigured: This control plane was started without the guard.
dockerGuard.restartRequired: The saved mode differs from the running one. Restart the control plane to apply it.
dockerGuard.readyToEnforce: Audit mode saw no would-be denials in the last {{days}} days. Enforce is likely safe.
dockerGuard.pinned: The mode is set by APP_DOCKER_GUARD on the server. Unset it to change the mode here.

githubAppOrg.addOrgHelp: GitHub shows the accounts you can install on. Pick the organization. If you are not an owner, GitHub sends the request to its owners.
githubAppOrg.privateTitle: This GitHub App is private, so GitHub only allows it on the account that owns it.
githubAppOrg.privateBody: To add an organization, open the App's Advanced settings, choose Make public (Any account), then come back and press Add organization. Or register a new App owned by the organization.
githubAppOrg.makePublic: Make the App public on GitHub
githubAppOrg.noSlug: This connection was registered before Levelrail could remember the App's install link. Reconnect the App above (or use manual setup) to enable Add organization here.

mobileDevices.title: Mobile devices
mobileDevices.description: Phones paired with this server. Each one holds its own expiring token that can read status and restart, deploy or roll back apps. It can never act as root, reveal secrets or approve sign-ins.
mobileDevices.pairFailed: Could not create a pairing code
mobileDevices.pairingHint: Enter this code in the mobile app, or open the link on the phone. It works once and expires at {{time}}.
mobileDevices.emptyDescription: Pair a device to check status and restart, deploy or roll back apps from your phone.
mobileDevices.revokeDescription: The phone loses access at once and has to be paired again.
